Either way, the two words connect.

quests.flowRule: Yod-coalescence (informal speech): When a word ending in /t/, /d/, /s/ or /z/ is followed by 'you' or 'your', the two sounds often merge into one: /t/+/j/ becomes /tʃ/ ('got you' sounds like 'gotcha'), /d/+/j/ becomes /dʒ/ ('did you' like 'didja'), /s/+/j/ becomes /ʃ/ and /z/+/j/ becomes /ʒ/. quests.flowRule: Place assimilation (informal speech): At the end of a word, /t/, /d/ and /n/ often take on the place of the next sound. Before /p b m/ they shift towards lip sounds (ten people sounds like 'tem people'; bad back like 'bab back'), and before /k g/ towards back-of-the-mouth sounds (in case like 'ing case').
